answer: Each applicant receives one copper bell cast around a single kernel of meteoric iron, hung in a dawn-lit tower. Each round, at dawn, the registry names a strike point; the holder strikes the bell and records its ring-down decay, matched to that bell's spectrum, and the next strike point is drawn from that decay plus the holder's key, so each strike must follow the last and no decay fits another bell. One more identity needs its own bell: $290 to cast and tune, plus 12 foundry-days cooling. 5,000 fakes would cost $1.45 million and 60,000 foundry-days; one bell never rings another bell's decay.
